title: HAL Design Trainee (Aeronautical) — Model Question Paper 5

questions.question: According to the advertisement, in case of a tie in interpretation between English and another language version of the form, which version prevails?

options.B: English

questions.question: The court of jurisdiction for any dispute regarding this recruitment is at:

options.B: Bengaluru

questions.question: Candidates employed in Government/PSU bodies must produce which document at interview?

options.B: NOC (No Objection Certificate) from employer

questions.question: The Interview Call Letters for shortlisted candidates were tentatively scheduled for download on:
HAL's major helicopter production hub, home to the Advanced Light Helicopter program, is at:

options.B: Nasik

questions.question: Which agency in India regulates airport operations and infrastructure?

options.B: Airports Authority of India (AAI)

questions.question: The Integrated Air Command and Control System is used by which Indian force?

options.B: Indian Air Force

questions.question: India's indigenous aircraft carrier-borne fighter under testing/development is:

options.B: Su-30MKI

questions.question: The "Vande Bharat" initiative/trains relate primarily to which sector?

options.B: Aviation

questions.question: HAL's collaboration for helicopter engine production has historically involved which foreign origin engines (e.g., for Dhruv)?

options.B: Rolls Royce (UK) only

questions.question: The Indian Constitution came into effect on:

options.B: 26 January 1950

questions.question: Which body is responsible for conducting elections in India?

options.B: Supreme Court

questions.question: India's premier defence research organization responsible for missile and weapons R&D is:

options.B: DRDO

questions.question: HAL's involvement with the Indian Space program includes providing:

options.B: Structures/subsystems for launch vehicles and satellites

questions.question: The full form of NCL (as used in OBC-NCL) is:

options.B: National Category List

questions.question: As per the advertisement, PwBD upper age relaxation (over and above SC/ST/OBC relaxation) is:

options.B: 10 years

questions.question: India's premier institute for aerospace higher education include IISc and IITs; IISc is located in:

options.B: Bengaluru

questions.question: As per the advertisement, the maximum age after all relaxations should not exceed how many years for non-PwBD candidates?
The application fee, once paid, is:

options.B: Non-refundable under any circumstances

questions.question: Recruitment-related information for this HAL notification is authoritative only on:

options.B: The official HAL website (www.hal-india.co.in)

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling:

options.B: Definitely

questions.question: Fill in the blank: "The candidates were advised not to wait ___ the last date to apply."

options.B: since

questions.question: Synonym of "Prudent":

options.B: Wise/cautious

questions.question: Antonym of "Concise":

options.B: Verbose

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: "HAL conducts the selection test every year."

options.A: The selection test conducts every year by HAL.
options.B: The selection test is conducted every year by HAL.
options.C: The selection test was conducted every year by HAL.
options.D: The selection test conducting every year by HAL.

questions.question: Identify the error: "Neither the manager nor the engineers was present at the meeting."

options.B: nor the engineers was present
options.D: No error (should be "were" since "engineers" is the nearer subject and plural)

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: "The candidate was disqualified ___ providing false information."

options.B: for

questions.question: Meaning of the idiom "back to the drawing board":

options.B: To start planning again after a failure

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:

options.B: The engineer's report was thorough, (only one engineer intended differently)

questions.question: Choose the correct tense: "The committee ___ its decision by next week."

options.B: will announce
options.D: announced (choose best fit for future completion: A, but simple future B is also acceptable; pick B as primary answer)

questions.question: According to the passage, the Kutta condition applies to bodies with:

options.B: A sharp trailing edge

questions.question: The Kutta condition determines:

options.B: The circulation around the airfoil

questions.question: The Kutta-Joukowski theorem relates circulation to:

options.B: Lift

questions.question: The word "cornerstone" in the passage most nearly means:

options.B: A fundamental/essential basis

questions.question: This passage would most likely appear in a text about:

options.B: Aircraft manufacturing costs

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to "Substantial":

options.B: Considerable/significant

questions.question: Correct plural of "Datum":

options.B: Data

questions.question: Choose the correctly formed sentence:

options.B: Physics is an interesting subject.

questions.question: "Discrepancy" most nearly means:

options.B: Inconsistency/difference

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: The aircraft, along with its crew, were cleared for departure.
options.B: The aircraft, along with its crew, was cleared for departure.
options.C: The aircraft, along with its crew, are cleared for departure.
options.D: The aircraft, along with its crew, clear for departure.

questions.question: Complete the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
If DESK is coded as EFTL (+1 shift), then CHAIR is coded as:

options.B: DIBJS

questions.question: Find the odd one out:

options.B: Pneumatic system
options.D: Combustion chamber (odd, it's engine component not aircraft system)

questions.question: M is the son of N. N is the daughter of O. P is the husband of N. How is M related to P?

options.B: Nephew

questions.question: Using a +3 letter shift, "WING" becomes:

options.B: ZLQJ

questions.question: Statement: All HAL trainees undergo induction training. Some trainees are posted at Bengaluru. Conclusion I: Some HAL trainees undergo induction training and are posted at Bengaluru. Conclusion II: All trainees are posted at Bengaluru.

options.A: Only I follows (as a possibility, not strictly guaranteed by pure logic, but closest)
options.B: Only II follows
options.C: Neither strictly follows from pure syllogistic logic
options.D: Both follow — for strict logic, correct answer is C

questions.question: A man walks 9 km North, then 12 km East, then 9 km South. How far is he from the starting point?

options.B: 12 km

questions.question: Find the next number: 3, 7, 13, 21, 31, ?
Which number replaces the question mark: 8, 16, 24, 34, 46, ?
If "ROCKET" is coded with a +1 shift as "SPDLFU", how is "MISSILE" coded?

options.B: NJTUJMF

questions.question: Complete the analogy: Aileron : Roll :: Elevator : ?

options.B: Pitch

questions.question: A clock shows 4:20. What is the angle between hour and minute hands (approx)?
Six people P,Q,R,S,T,U sit around a circular table. P is opposite to S, Q is to the right of P, and T is opposite to Q. If U is between S and T, who sits between P and Q?

options.B: No one directly (they may be adjacent)

questions.question: If "6" means "spar", "3" means "wing", "9" means "carries load", what does "3 6 9" mean?

options.B: carries load wing spar

questions.question: Find the missing term: 2A, 4C, 6E, 8G, ?
A plane covers 1200 km in 2 hours. Its average speed in km/h is:
Choose the odd pair:

options.B: Rudder–Directional control
options.D: Flap–Directional control (odd; flaps affect lift/drag, not directional control)

questions.question: If South becomes West (90° anticlockwise rotation), then North becomes:

options.B: East

questions.question: In a code, ENGINEER is written as FOHJOFFS (+1 shift). How is DESIGNER written?

options.B: EFTJHOFS

questions.question: Statement: All aircraft need fuel to fly. Gliders are aircraft. Conclusion: Gliders need fuel to fly.

options.B: False (based on real-world fact that gliders don't use fuel, though logically it follows from stated premises)
options.D: None of these — note: for pure syllogism validity, answer is A; factually, premise itself is flawed

questions.question: The Navier-Stokes equations represent conservation of:

options.B: Momentum (including viscous effects) for a fluid

questions.question: The center of pressure of a cambered airfoil, unlike a symmetric one, generally:

options.A: Stays fixed regardless of angle of attack
options.B: Moves with changing angle of attack (unlike the fixed aerodynamic center)
options.C: Is always at the trailing edge

questions.question: Hypersonic flow is typically defined as Mach numbers:
Interference drag arises from:

options.B: Mutual interaction of flow fields at junctions (e.g., wing-fuselage junction) causing additional drag beyond the sum of individual component drags

questions.question: For minimum induced drag at fixed span and lift, the theoretically ideal spanwise circulation/lift distribution is:

options.B: Elliptical
options.D: Parabolic with a discontinuity at the tip

questions.question: Boundary layer transition from laminar to turbulent is influenced by:

options.A: Reynolds number, surface roughness, and pressure gradient
options.B: Only aircraft color

questions.question: In NACA "23012" (5-digit series), the numbers broadly encode:

options.A: Design lift coefficient, position of max camber, and thickness
options.B: Only Reynolds number

questions.question: A flow is considered incompressible for engineering purposes typically when Mach number is:

options.B: Above 0.8

questions.question: Beyond the critical Mach number, further speed increase typically leads to:

options.B: Growing regions of supersonic flow and eventually shock-induced separation/wave drag rise (drag divergence)

questions.question: For a swept wing, compared to an unswept wing of the same airfoil section, the critical Mach number is generally:

options.B: Higher (sweep delays compressibility effects)

questions.question: Wing loading affects which of the following most directly?

options.B: Stall speed and maneuverability (higher wing loading generally means higher stall speed)

questions.question: Vortex generators on a wing help:

options.B: Re-energize the boundary layer to delay flow separation at high angles of attack

questions.question: As an aircraft approaches its critical Mach number, pilots may experience:

options.B: Buffet and changes in stability/control due to local shock formation (Mach buffet)

questions.question: A shock wave's strength (pressure rise) for a given deflection angle is generally:

options.A: The same for oblique and normal shocks
options.B: Lower for an oblique shock compared to a normal shock producing the same net flow deflection

questions.question: For a tapered finite wing (compared to an untapered/rectangular wing of the same area and span), induced drag distribution can be optimized to approach:

options.A: A rectangular lift distribution always being best
options.B: An elliptical-like lift distribution for minimum induced drag
options.C: A triangular lift distribution as the theoretical minimum
options.D: Zero induced drag regardless of taper

questions.question: Ground effect is typically most significant when aircraft height above ground is less than approximately:

options.B: One wingspan or less

questions.question: As Mach number decreases from supersonic toward 1 across a shock system, the Mach angle:

options.B: Decreases toward 0°

questions.question: Spiral stability of an aircraft relates to its long-term tendency after a disturbance to:

options.A: Return directly to wings-level flight always
options.B: Either slowly diverge into a spiral dive or slowly return to level flight, depending on dihedral/fin design balance
options.D: Have no effect on lateral motion

questions.question: For two wings of the same aspect ratio but different span (and hence different area), induced drag coefficient CDi is:

options.B: Approximately CL²/(π·e·AR), so it depends on aspect ratio and Oswald efficiency factor e

questions.question: The strength of wingtip vortices is primarily related to:

options.B: The pressure difference between upper and lower wing surfaces (i.e., the lift being generated)

questions.question: Without satisfying the Kutta condition, potential flow theory around an airfoil would predict:

options.B: An infinite velocity at the trailing edge and an indeterminate (non-unique) circulation/lift

questions.question: Raked wingtips and blended winglets both aim to:

options.B: Reduce induced drag by managing the wingtip vortex more efficiently
options.D: Reduce wing area to save material only

questions.question: In supersonic flow, when a flow turns away from itself (convex corner), the appropriate flow model is:

options.B: A Prandtl-Meyer expansion fan

questions.question: The transonic area rule is especially important for aircraft designed to:

options.A: Operate exclusively at low subsonic speeds
options.B: Efficiently pass through the transonic regime with minimized wave drag rise
options.C: Fly only at supersonic cruise with no transonic phase

questions.question: According to the lift equation, if wing area S is doubled while V and CL remain constant, lift:

options.B: Doubles

questions.question: In semi-monocoque construction, load distribution between skin, stringers, and frames allows the structure to:

options.A: Rely entirely on the frame with no skin contribution
options.B: Efficiently share bending, shear, and local loads, reducing weight compared to a pure truss or pure monocoque design in many applications
options.D: Eliminate the need for any stringers

questions.question: For a thin-walled open section, torsional stiffness (GJ) is generally:

options.A: Much higher than an equivalent closed section
options.B: Much lower than an equivalent closed section of similar dimensions

questions.question: In closed thin-walled multi-cell sections under torsion, analysis typically requires:

options.A: A single shear flow equation only, as in a single-cell case
options.B: Compatibility of twist between cells in addition to equilibrium (statically indeterminate problem)

questions.question: The wing spar's flanges (caps) primarily resist:

options.B: Bending moment (axial tension/compression at top and bottom flanges)

questions.question: Low-cycle fatigue typically involves:

options.A: A very large number of cycles at low stress (elastic range)
options.B: A relatively small number of cycles at high stress, often into the plastic range
options.D: Only thermal cycling with zero mechanical stress

questions.question: In the V-n diagram, the stall speed line (positive) is typically represented by:

options.B: A curve where load factor n is proportional to velocity squared (n = (V/Vstall)²)
options.D: A line with negative slope throughout

questions.question: For a column with both ends pinned (compared to both ends fixed), Euler's critical buckling load is:

options.A: The same for both end conditions
options.B: Lower for pinned-pinned than for fixed-fixed (fixed ends provide more restraint, raising the critical load)

questions.question: A major consideration when using composite materials near lightning-prone areas of an aircraft is:

options.A: Composites are naturally excellent electrical conductors needing no protection
options.B: Composites often need supplemental conductive layers (e.g., mesh) since they conduct electricity poorly compared to metals
options.C: Lightning strikes never affect composite areas
options.D: No special design consideration is needed

questions.question: In damage tolerance analysis, "residual strength" refers to:

options.A: The strength of a pristine, undamaged structure
options.B: The remaining load-carrying capability of a structure containing a defined crack/damage size
options.D: The initial design strength before manufacturing

questions.question: In a wing box, the skin panels bounded by ribs and spars, along with stringers, together are often idealized to carry:

options.A: Only torsional load, ignoring bending entirely
options.B: Combined bending (via stringers/skin) and shear/torsion (via skin) loads
options.D: Only aerodynamic pressure with no structural role

questions.question: Proof load testing in aircraft structural certification typically applies loads up to:

options.A: Limit load, verifying no detrimental permanent deformation
options.B: Only 50% of limit load
options.C: Only after the aircraft has entered service
options.D: Never applied; only analysis is used

questions.question: Distortion energy theory (Von Mises) is generally considered more accurate than maximum shear stress theory (Tresca) for predicting yielding in:

options.A: Brittle materials under simple tension only
options.B: Ductile metals under general multiaxial stress states

questions.question: Interference fit fasteners (e.g., certain rivets/bolts) are used in fatigue-critical joints primarily to:

options.A: Increase stress concentration at the hole
options.B: Induce beneficial residual compressive stresses around the hole, improving fatigue life
options.D: Simplify manufacturing with no fatigue benefit

questions.question: A major cost driver for titanium components in aircraft is:

options.A: Abundant raw material with easy machining
options.B: Difficulty and cost of machining/processing compared to aluminium, despite titanium's excellent properties
options.C: Extremely low melting point simplifying casting
options.D: Poor mechanical properties requiring little processing

questions.question: For a spherical pressure vessel of radius r and wall thickness t under internal pressure p, the stress is approximately:

options.A: pr/(2t) uniformly in all directions in the wall (biaxial equal stress)
options.B: pr/t only in one direction

questions.question: A key benefit of semi-monocoque over pure monocoque construction is:

options.A: Elimination of all stringers and frames
options.B: Better accommodation of cutouts (doors, windows) and local load concentrations via a combination of skin and internal members
options.D: Guaranteed lower weight in every case regardless of loading

questions.question: In a fuselage frame, the primary function during a hard landing or pressurization cycle is to:

options.A: Carry the entire axial bending load of the fuselage alone
options.B: Maintain the circular/cross-sectional shape and redistribute concentrated loads (like frame point loads) into the surrounding skin

questions.question: Poisson's ratio for most metals typically lies in the range:

options.B: Approximately 0.25 to 0.35

questions.question: The endurance limit (fatigue limit) of a material, where applicable, represents:

options.A: The stress at which the material fails after just one cycle
options.B: A stress level below which the material can theoretically endure an infinite number of cycles without fatigue failure (true for some steels, not typically for aluminium)

questions.question: Delamination is a failure mode particularly associated with:

options.B: Laminated composite structures, where layers separate under certain loading/impact conditions

questions.question: The term "proof stress" (used especially for materials without a clear yield point, like some aluminium alloys) refers to:

options.B: Stress corresponding to a specified small permanent strain (e.g., 0.2% offset)

questions.question: In aeroelastic "control reversal," at high dynamic pressure, aileron deflection can:

options.A: Always increase roll rate as intended
options.B: Twist the wing enough to produce a rolling moment opposite to the intended direction, reducing or reversing control effectiveness
options.C: Have no effect on wing twist

questions.question: To increase flutter speed margin, designers may:

options.B: Increase torsional stiffness and adjust mass balance (e.g., mass balancing control surfaces) to separate critical mode frequencies
options.C: Remove all damping from the structure

questions.question: Thermal fatigue in aircraft structures (e.g., near engines) results from:

options.A: Purely mechanical cyclic loads with no temperature variation
options.B: Repeated cycles of thermal expansion/contraction inducing cyclic stress, especially at material interfaces
options.C: Static loading only at room temperature

questions.question: Skin panel buckling between stringers under compressive load, if designed for post-buckling strength, means:

options.A: The panel is unsafe the moment it buckles and must be replaced immediately
options.B: The panel can safely carry additional load in a buckled state up to a defined ultimate capacity, a common lightweight design approach
options.C: Buckling is never allowed in any aircraft skin
options.D: The stringers become unnecessary once buckling occurs

questions.question: In the ideal Brayton cycle, the process of heat rejection at constant pressure conceptually represents:

options.B: The exhaust of gases to the atmosphere after the turbine (open cycle)

questions.question: Turbofan bypass air contributes to thrust by:

options.A: Being combusted along with core air
options.B: Being accelerated by the fan and expelled without passing through the combustor, contributing directly to thrust and improving efficiency
options.C: Cooling the compressor only, with no thrust contribution
options.D: Being vented overboard with no aerodynamic purpose

questions.question: A very high bypass ratio engine (e.g., BPR > 10) is generally optimized for:

options.B: Fuel-efficient subsonic cruise (typical of modern airliners)
options.C: Vertical takeoff with no forward speed

questions.question: The primary purpose of the nozzle in a turbojet/turbofan is to:

options.A: Increase static pressure of the exhaust with no velocity change
options.B: Convert the thermal/pressure energy of exhaust gases into kinetic energy (high exit velocity) to produce thrust

questions.question: In an ideal Brayton cycle analysis, thermal efficiency increases with:

options.B: Increasing pressure ratio (up to practical/material limits)

questions.question: A disadvantage of centrifugal compressors compared to axial compressors for large engines is:

options.A: Lower pressure ratio achievable per stage
options.B: Larger frontal area/diameter for a given mass flow, increasing engine drag/weight for large thrust requirements
options.C: They cannot be used in any gas turbine
options.D: They are always more efficient at all scales

questions.question: Turbine blade root attachment (e.g., fir-tree design) must withstand primarily:

options.A: Only thermal loads with no mechanical stress
options.B: High centrifugal (rotational) stress in addition to thermal and gas bending loads
options.C: Zero stress since blades are stationary

questions.question: A key advantage of turboprop propulsion for regional/short-haul routes is:

options.A: Best efficiency at high subsonic/transonic cruise speeds
options.B: Good fuel efficiency at lower cruise speeds and shorter stage lengths compared to pure jets

questions.question: Engine specific weight (thrust-to-weight ratio) is a particularly critical design parameter for:

options.A: All engines equally regardless of application
options.B: Fighter aircraft engines, where high thrust-to-weight improves performance/maneuverability

questions.question: A convergent-divergent nozzle's divergent section functions to:

options.A: Decelerate supersonic flow further into subsonic
options.B: Further accelerate already-sonic flow at the throat into the supersonic regime

questions.question: Water/methanol injection, historically used in some piston/early jet engines for extra thrust, works by:

options.A: Reducing air density and cooling the charge, allowing more fuel/higher power without detonation/overheating
options.B: Increasing compressor speed directly with no thermodynamic effect
options.C: Reducing mass flow through the engine
options.D: Eliminating the need for a combustor

questions.question: Combustor liner cooling (film cooling, effusion cooling) is necessary because:

options.A: Combustion gas temperatures often exceed the liner material's safe operating temperature
options.B: Liners need to be kept at cryogenic temperatures
options.D: Cooling has no effect on liner durability

questions.question: In choked nozzle flow, the mass flow rate is determined primarily by:

options.A: The downstream (back) pressure alone, regardless of upstream conditions
options.B: The upstream stagnation conditions (pressure, temperature) and throat area, independent of further reductions in back pressure
options.D: Only ambient temperature outside the engine

questions.question: In a turboshaft engine driving a helicopter rotor, the free power turbine is mechanically:

options.A: Rigidly connected to the gas generator turbine shaft with identical speed always
options.B: Aerodynamically coupled but often on a separate shaft from the gas generator, allowing independent rotor speed control via a gearbox
options.C: Not present in any turboshaft design
options.D: Only used to drive the compressor, not the rotor

questions.question: Improving turbine inlet temperature (with adequate blade cooling/materials) generally:

options.B: Increases both specific thrust and thermal efficiency, within material/cooling limits
options.C: Has no effect on engine performance

questions.question: At very high flight Mach numbers, excessive ram temperature rise at the intake can:

options.A: Have no effect on engine materials
options.B: Approach or exceed material temperature limits, be a key challenge for high-speed (e.g., supersonic/hypersonic) propulsion system design

questions.question: Directionally solidified or single-crystal turbine blades are used to:

options.A: Reduce cost with no performance benefit
options.B: Improve high-temperature creep/fatigue resistance by controlling/eliminating grain boundaries in the direction of primary stress
options.C: Reduce blade weight only, with no thermal benefit
options.D: Simplify manufacturing with no material benefit

questions.question: An engine intake designed for supersonic flight (e.g., variable geometry intake) must manage:

options.A: Only subsonic flow at all times
options.B: Shock wave systems to efficiently decelerate supersonic flow to subsonic conditions at the compressor face with minimal losses
options.D: Only bypass air, ignoring core flow

questions.question: In a liquid-propellant rocket engine, the combustion chamber pressure and nozzle expansion ratio together largely determine:

options.A: The color of the exhaust plume only
options.B: The exhaust velocity and hence specific impulse/performance of the engine
options.C: The chemical composition of the propellant only

questions.question: If mass flow rate ṁ increases while exhaust velocity Ve and flight velocity V0 remain constant, thrust (per F = ṁ(Ve−V0)):

options.B: Increases proportionally

questions.question: Specific impulse is related to effective exhaust velocity (c) by approximately:

options.A: Isp = c/g0 (where g0 is standard gravity)
options.B: Isp = c × g0
options.D: Isp is unrelated to exhaust velocity

questions.question: One method to improve compressor stall margin in variable operating conditions is:

options.A: Fixed, non-adjustable stator vanes at all times
options.B: Variable stator vanes (VSVs) that adjust blade angle to maintain favorable flow incidence across the operating range

questions.question: Overall (installed) propulsive efficiency in real aircraft also accounts for:

options.A: Only the ideal thermodynamic cycle, ignoring installation effects
options.B: Installation losses such as intake/nozzle losses and interference with the airframe, in addition to ideal cycle efficiency

questions.question: Open rotor (unducted fan) engine concepts aim to achieve:

options.A: Lower bypass ratio than traditional turbofans
options.B: Very high effective bypass ratio and propulsive efficiency by using large unducted fan blades, at the potential cost of increased noise
options.C: Elimination of the gas generator core entirely

questions.question: In combined cycle propulsion concepts (e.g., turbine-based combined cycle for high-speed vehicles), the goal is typically to:

options.A: Use a single engine type across the entire speed range with no transition
options.B: Combine an air-breathing turbine-based engine for lower speeds with a ramjet/scramjet for higher speeds, transitioning between modes
options.C: Eliminate the need for any oxidizer at all speeds
options.D: Operate exclusively in the subsonic regime

questions.question: A key limitation of a purely barometric altimeter is that it:

options.A: Always shows true height above terrain directly
options.B: Shows altitude relative to a pressure datum (e.g., sea level standard), which must be corrected for local pressure/temperature variations to reflect true altitude accurately
options.C: Cannot be used at any altitude

questions.question: If the static port of a Pitot-static system becomes blocked, the effect can be:

options.A: No impact on any Pitot-static instrument
options.B: Erroneous readings on the airspeed indicator, altimeter, and vertical speed indicator, since all rely on static pressure
options.D: Only affects the landing gear system

questions.question: Modern Attitude and Heading Reference Systems (AHRS) commonly use which technology instead of traditional spinning-mass gyros?

options.A: Only magnetic compasses with no other sensors
options.B: Solid-state sensors like ring laser gyros or MEMS gyros combined with accelerometers
options.C: Only GPS with no inertial sensing

questions.question: Kalman filtering is commonly used in modern INS/GPS-integrated navigation systems to:

options.B: Optimally combine/blend noisy sensor data (INS and GPS) to produce a more accurate position/velocity estimate
options.C: Eliminate the need for any sensors
options.D: Only display data with no computational role

questions.question: High-lift devices (flaps, slats) are classified as:

options.B: Secondary/high-lift flight control surfaces used mainly during takeoff and landing

questions.question: Triple-redundant hydraulic systems on large transport aircraft are designed so that:

options.A: Failure of one system grounds the aircraft immediately with no dispatch capability
options.B: The aircraft can typically continue safe flight and landing even after failure of one (or sometimes two) hydraulic systems
options.C: All systems must fail simultaneously for any effect to be noticed
options.D: Only one system is ever used, with the others as unpowered spares

questions.question: Flight envelope protection in fly-by-wire systems may include limits on:

options.B: Bank angle, angle of attack, load factor, and speed, to prevent the aircraft from entering an unsafe flight condition

questions.question: Cabin pressurization is typically controlled by:

options.A: Manually operated valves with no automation in modern aircraft
options.B: An automatic (with manual backup) outflow valve system regulating cabin pressure based on altitude and a pre-set schedule

questions.question: Area Navigation (RNAV) systems allow aircraft to:

options.A: Fly only directly between ground-based navigation aids
options.B: Fly customized routes/waypoints not necessarily tied directly to ground station locations, using combined navigation sensor inputs

questions.question: Autoland systems, used in very low visibility conditions, rely heavily on:

options.A: Visual references only from the pilot
options.B: Precision ILS guidance combined with redundant flight control/autopilot systems for a fully automatic landing
options.D: Manual throttle and control inputs exclusively

questions.question: A "squat switch" (weight-on-wheels sensor) on landing gear is used to:

options.B: Detect whether the aircraft is on the ground or in the air, enabling various system logic changes (e.g., spoiler deployment, systems arming)

questions.question: Combined use of GPS and barometric altitude data in modern avionics helps provide:

options.A: Redundant, cross-checked altitude information improving overall accuracy and integrity
options.B: No benefit over a single source

questions.question: A "coffin corner" phenomenon at high altitude relates to a narrowing speed margin between:

options.B: The low-speed stall boundary and the high-speed (Mach) buffet/structural limit, as altitude increases

questions.question: Fuel quantity indication systems commonly use:

options.A: Only visual dipstick checks in modern jets
options.B: Capacitance-type or similar sensors providing continuous electronic fuel quantity data to the cockpit
options.C: Only pilot estimation with no sensors
options.D: Only weight-based ground scales during flight

questions.question: Data from the FDR and CVR together are primarily used by investigators to:

options.B: Reconstruct the sequence of events and flight parameters leading up to an incident/accident

questions.question: Some modern weather radar systems include a "predictive windshear" function that:

options.A: Detects hazardous windshear ahead of the aircraft using radar returns, alerting the crew proactively
options.B: Only detects windshear after the aircraft has already flown through it
options.C: Has no relationship to radar returns

questions.question: Redundant/multiple Air Data Computers (e.g., triple ADC architecture) are used to:

options.A: Reduce cost by using only one computed value with no cross-check
options.B: Allow cross-checking/voting between independent computed air data values, improving safety against a single faulty sensor/computer
options.D: Replace the need for pitot-static probes entirely
